name: Screen
purpose: Lays out one screen of the app: the navigation bar at the top, the content, which scrolls, and the tab bar or a button stack at the bottom. Write a screen's components inside it in order, top to bottom.

origin.notes: How iOS lays out a screen under the app's SwiftUI views: a ScrollView of content 16pt in from the sides, under the navigation bar, with room for the status bar and home indicator. The app sets only the background: fills.surfaceBackground, or fills.surfaceModal for a modal. What is pinned to the bottom, such as the app's button stack, is a component of its own.

background.description: page: the app's pale blue, for screens in its sections. modal: white, for a screen presented over them, such as a question or a confirmation.

inputs.content: The screen's components, top to bottom. A <govuk-app-nav-bar> goes at the top and sticks there. A <govuk-app-tab-bar> goes at the bottom of the content and floats over it. An element with slot="footer", usually a <govuk-app-button-stack>, is pinned below the content. Everything else is the content, 16pt in from the sides and 16pt apart, and scrolls.

rules: Put a screen directly in a <govuk-app>, and give the root a size: the screen fills it, and scrolls inside it.
Use one screen for each screen of a journey. In a prototype of several pages, put each on its own page.
Give a screen either a tab bar or a button stack, not both: the app hides the tab bar on screens that ask the user to act.
Use the modal background for screens presented over the app, such as a sign-out confirmation, and the page background for the rest.
